AW-STUDY-0053 · Charms · Winchester board · demo prep

Where can I earn my charms?

A chest that holds every charm the way the coin chest holds Daddy's memories. Open it and the places that can pay a charm start to glint on the Winchester board. Every earned charm then lives in a jewellery box under a little glass dome. This page also fixes the style of the mission board the demo will build, and the zoom that takes you from the board into a mission. The stage below is playable: open the chest, place the Moon and Ranch tiles, tap the noticeboard in the town square.

Design card

What she needs to feel"There's a sparkly thing over the science lab! I want it." Wanting, then finding, never a to-do list.
How would the character know?Charms glint over the place that pays them, like a lantern left in a window. Bub can lead her there by his paw prints. The chest is a real object she carries: an empty velvet slot is a charm she hasn't found.
ModeChest slot shape: diegetic. Glints over places: spatial (only she can see them). Quest words: one sentence on the place itself. No overlay except the chest's count on the chest.
Who it's forPlayer (the child) for the glints and chest. Grown-up view lists every charm with where and how it is earned.
The whole game adaptsOpening the chest: a small harp glissando, the town's lamps lean toward the nearest unearned place, Bub's tail wag speeds up near it. An earned charm drops into its slot with the same golden pickup as a gold coin.

The board, the chest, the tiles, the noticeboard

Start: the seven-tile Winchester board. Bottom left, the charm chest. Bottom right, the tile bag. In the town square by the high school (centre, where the three zones meet), the noticeboard.

Charm chest

Question 1

"Show me where I can earn my charms": four ways, same board

Recommended, the default

A · Glints over the places

Open the chest and each place that can pay a charm wears that charm, bobbing. Earned charms stop glinting. Closing the chest puts the town back to how it was. Spatial mode: only she can see them.

The hint

B · Bub's paw prints

"Ask bub": paw prints run from the backpack to the nearest charm and bub sits there. Diegetic, since a dog leading you somewhere is something the characters see too. Best for the youngest and for being stuck.

Recommended with A · Evan's idea

D · The locked card

What you haven't earned is a locked card: the charm's card, greyed and dull. Tap it and you see the disabled version of the card plus one button, "Show me where". It flies the camera there and sets a low-poly padlock on the spot that unlocks it. The padlock is a real game-ready model (padlock.glb, 158 triangles, three named parts, flat shaded), not a drawn icon.

The aim

C · Tap an empty slot

One empty velvet slot picked: a column of lantern light lands on its place and one sentence hangs there. Everything else stays quiet. The most precise, and it works at any zoom.

How they fit together: tapping the chest gives A. Tapping an empty slot opens D, its locked card. "Show me where" on that card gives C's lantern light plus the padlock. The paw button inside the chest gives B. A shows everything, D explains one and takes you to it, B walks you to it. Charms that need the Moon tile show as a ghost on the empty Moon slot ("needs a Moon tile") instead of vanishing, so wanting them starts the unlock.

Question 2

The charm chest: eleven now, just like the coins

Recommended

The chest

Eleven velvet slots shaped like their charms. An earned charm drops in with the same golden pickup as a gold coin; the lid shows the count as engraved numerals ("4 of 10"), the only number in sight. Tap a charm and the camera comes close, as in the backpack.

Like the coins, in four ways

  • Same store. earnCharm(id) in simulations/backpack.mjs; the chest only reads earnedCharms().
  • Same pickup. The golden reward animation from inventory.mjs.
  • Same place. Beside the coin pile at the backpack, and the chest button on the board.
  • Same rule. You can't lose one, and the empty slot shows what you're missing, not a number you failed.

Eleven, and it can grow. The plain gold coin charm (first-memory) has been removed from CHARMS (Backpack thread), so the eleven slots are the whole set. Moon cheese is repeatable and takes one slot, with up to two on the keychain. The jewellery box's "put in the box" toggle should call putInBox(id, yes) / inBox(id) from backpack.mjs; keychain() then leaves boxed charms off the worn backpack.

Question 3

The jewellery box with encasement

Recommended

A · Drawer box with glass domes

Tap a case: the dome tips up, the charm lifts and turns. Tap "hang it" and it goes on the bag; two at a time (the backpack's keychain limit). A third makes the first case shake: "two at a time". Empty cases show the charm's shadow and a pip with the place's zone colour.

Alternative

B · Wall shadow-box

Each charm pinned in a frame behind one big sheet of glass, brass plate under it. Prettier hung in her room; harder to lift and dress with. Keep it for the bedroom wall, not the backpack.

Evan's core loop · the charm track

Charms unlock blueprints, blueprints unlock tiles

The overland loop: explore the world, find the minigames, collect world charms, unlock card blueprints, and grow the board with new tiles. This progression is the charm track. Other tracks can sit beside it later. Each rung below lights up as you earn its charms in the stage above ("Pretend I earned one" works too).

This grouping is my proposal, ready for Evan to rearrange. The data is one list (TRACK), so a rung can change its charms, blueprint or tile without touching the layout. Update from the Winchester thread: the Science tile plan was cancelled and the high school stays in the Downtown centre hex, so the first rung is parked until Evan decides. This study does not edit Winchester files.

Evan, 6:51 PM · drafted, not in the game yet

Floating charms, like the hidden packages in GTA 3

Charms are the only reward, and they hang in the world as spinning, glowing pickups. Walk into one and it flies to your chest. Try it: the board below is the Winchester sample, every charm floats in a hidden nook near its place. Move the pointer over the board and a small ring shimmers faster the closer you are to an uncollected charm (the hot and cold feel, with no arrow and no list). Tap a floating charm to collect it.

How it behaves

  • Look. The charm's own hero model, slowly spinning and bobbing, a soft gold glow and a ground shadow that breathes.
  • Find. Two kinds. Won charms (tardigrade, floppy, toy car, rocket, moon cheese, star) appear at the place when you finish the minigame, as a drop. Found charms (bub, coffee cup, brass key) sit hidden in nooks until you explore to them. The Heart never floats: it comes by itself.
  • Hint. Meta only: a faint chime that rises in pitch as you near one, and the sparkle ring above. No minimap dots. The chest's locked cards still give a "Show me where" for anyone who wants it.
  • Pickup. Walk in, golden pickup animation (the coin one), the charm flies into the chest and the slot lights.

Placement (a proposal for the hex city thread)

These spots are Winchester edits, so I only list them; I touched no town files. Offsets are from the place's door, in metres on the town's local grid: café window box (-2, +1), café cellar steps (0, -1.5), the back corner of the skate park beside the café, Abbie's pink tree house (spot abbie-daddy-side.abbieTree), the school roof ladder (0, +3; the school model has no ladder yet), the curb where the black truck parks outside the French bakery (bakery-curb). The lab spot is dropped: the science adventure is parked. Town code to use: AbbieTown.board.heightAt(x,y) for ground height, board.obstaclesNear(x,y,r) to keep pickups clear of houses and trees, AbbieTown.stage.tiles[hexId].spots[id] for positions. This preview's board still draws the lab as a mock. Moon outpost and the coaster follow their own tiles.

Not built: the in-game spinner (a shared charm-pickup world sprite), the proximity chime, and the drop when a minigame ends.

Question 4 · hand-off to the demo

The mission board

Recommended · the demo builds this

A · Town noticeboard

A cork board in a painted-wood frame with a brass plate, standing in the town square by the school. Each mission is a die-cut card (the Cards v3 face) pinned with a red pin: a little picture of the place, one sentence, and the charm stamp it pays. Locked: greyed, with a "needs the Moon tile" tag. Done: green tag. The big card at the bottom is the Moon Mission. Diegetic: a noticeboard characters read too.

Alternative

B · A hand of cards on the table

The same cards fanned like the card hand. Quicker to read, and it is an overlay across the lower third of the board. It fails the "nothing masks the world" check at phone width.

Echo, always on

C · Pennants on the places

Each open mission flies a small flag over its place on the board, so the board itself says where the work is. Not a replacement; it's what A's cards echo into the world after you've read them.

The transition: zoom into the board, smoke and mirrors

0.0 – 0.9 sTap a card. The camera dollies toward that place on the board (the stage above does it; tap the noticeboard).
0.5 – 1.3 sA cartoon smoke puff blooms on the place only (under a quarter of the screen). The old board and the new scene swap behind it, just as the paint-world splash hid its swap.
1.3 sThe puff clears on the mission's own opening shot, in the place's dialect (café basement, lab, Moon base). No fade to white, no full-screen cover.
ReturnFinish or leave: the reverse puff on the board, and the charm drops into the chest if it was earned.
Hand-off · for "Demo flow and opening tour"

What the demo builds from this study

  1. Board. Start on the seven-tile Winchester board: three zones plus the high school at the centre, no minimap logo there. Downtown, Ani's side and Abbie and Daddy's side each get a minimap logo (this page's glyphs: cup, waves, rocket and star).
  2. Tile bag. Moon and Ranch tiles as two tokens bottom right. A placed tile snaps to the nearest open edge and takes the height of the neighbour's edge, then slopes off, so contour lines run straight across the seam (the stage shows the seam flash). Real game: the Moon token is the prize of the Moon Mission; the demo may start with it in the bag.
  3. Chest. Bottom-left object as styled here; opens the earn map (A/B/C above). Reads earnedCharms(); slots are the eleven in the table; the chest reads CHARMS, so a new charm is a new slot.
  4. Mission board. Option A above, in the town square. Cards in order: Coffee shop basement, Science lab, Moon base mining (locked until a Moon tile is on the board), then the large Moon Mission card. Finishing the Moon Mission earns the rocket and the moon-key charms and gives the Moon token.
  5. Zoom. Use the timeline above; the puff is a sprite on the place, not a full-screen mask. The game-feel world-cover check must still pass.
  6. Tour. The kids' tour (Abbie and Ani) should name the chest in one line: "Everything you find on a mission lands in your charm chest." Tour decision for the chest and the mission board: yes.

How this fits the code, and what is still open

  • Reads only: CHARMS, earnedCharms(), keychain() from simulations/backpack.mjs. No Winchester town files were touched. This page is a mock on its own SVG board; it has no game code.
  • Charm pictures are the hero charms from the Midjourney sheet (same as the backpack). Moon cheese has no hero picture yet, so it's a drawn wedge here.
  • The Moon Mission opens on a circle: the Moon tile unlocks from the mission, but moon mining needs the tile. Demo rules start with the token in the bag; real rules give it as the prize. The toggle above shows both.
  • Not yet built: the chest and noticeboard inside /town, the real tile-conforming terrain, and ElevenLabs voice for the tour.
